newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Serbian opposition leader's wife returns home.
newsitem.headline: Serbian opposition leader's wife returns home.

text.p: The wife of Serbian opposition leader Vuk Draskovic returned home on Friday after she disappeared amid allegations that state authorities had kidnapped her.
A spokesman for the Serbian Renewal Movement (SPO) told Reuters Draskovic's wife Danica had called from home saying she had been released and was safe and well.
The spokesman declined to give further details, saying the party would release a statement later.
The SPO leader accused the authorities on Thursday of snatching her hours after she made remarks seen as urging her supporters to resort to violence.
Serbian police denied they had arrested Danica Draskovic and it was impossible to independently verify the allegations.
State television and radio repeatedly broadcast comments Danica Draskovic made to reporters on Thursday evening.
Asked if "terrorist" groups should be formed, she replied: "I can't wait for this to happen".
State television used her statement to corroborate its portrayal of the opposition movement as bent on resorting to violence to achieve its goals ahead of run-off elections on November 27.

The alleged kidnapping and subsequent release followed days of protests in which thousands of opposition supporters marched through the streets of Belgrade protesting what they say was widespread fraud denying them victory in Sunday's local elections.
